1.why: Screens use a legible sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and ample whitespace, though letter spacing is standard rather than explicitly generous.

2.why: All instructional prose is short, upright, sentence-case text with no italics, all-caps styling, or dense paragraphs (the only all-caps string is the setup secret itself, not an instruction).

3.why: Content is a single narrow centred column with large text and full-width buttons that should reflow to phone width, though only desktop-size screenshots were available to inspect.

4.why: Instructions are single short plain-language sentences such as 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret'.

5.why: The six-digit code field shows no placeholder or worked example, and the pre-filled email/phone values are stored registered data rather than examples of expected input.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long block; the longest passage is a two-line note about the simulated code being available in the browser console.

7.why: The 32-character setup secret is displayed as plain selectable text in a highlighted box so it can be copied, but no one-tap copy button is provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent is offered; the page explicitly tells the user to 'Choose manual entry and enter this setup secret'.

9.why: The inputs are ordinary text fields with no visible one-time-code autofill hint or any other indication of password-manager or autofill support, so neither confirmation nor refutation is observable.

10.why: Each screen pairs a bold task heading with a single high-contrast blue primary button, though no step counter indicates the user's position in the enrolment flow.

11.why: Every screen requests exactly one primary action (Verify and continue / Set up authenticator app / Confirm code), with Log out styled as a clearly secondary option.

12.why: After each action the log appends a plain status line (e.g., 'identity verification completed') and the following screen states the next task, though log phrasing is somewhat technical.

13.why: The form remains active after the failed attempt so retry is possible without visible penalty, but there are no reveal/hide controls and no way to re-request a code.

14.why: The red message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blame but never states the actual problem (wrong, expired, or malformed code) or how to fix it beyond retrying.

15.why: Nothing times the user's reading, but the required code is explicitly a time-bound TOTP value with no countdown, stated grace period, or extended entry window, so entry time is not generous.
